adopted: Prepare no-solve CPU readout of stored center100/150/200 point traces: availability, coordinates, sample times/components, prefix agreement and local tail diagnostic. Review actual metadata before spectral interpretation.
rejected_or_qualified: Point field ratios, dimensionless transmitted power changes and derivatives per nm are different units; do not compare as error bounds without a derived mapping.
Real optical traces require Nyquist consideration of carrier plus relevant bandwidth, not bandwidth alone.
Different prefixes do not alone prove stochastic nondeterminism; numerical execution or duration-dependent settings require checking. Agreement establishes consistency only at sampled points.
Quiet point monitors cannot exclude global/port temporal truncation effects.
Point traces do not establish exact port DFT convention or flux/modal normalization.
No automatic declaration that stationary adjoint is categorically wrong; finite-time endpoint terms may matter and require convergence/derivation.
Reject final contradictory claim that an adjoint becomes plausibly correct when mismatch is larger than FD spreads.
Do not adopt suggested fixed150 adjoint release or arbitrary two-solve cap as a scientific gate.
Original one-repeat scale is not a noise bound at200ps.
One-minute extraction is an estimate dependent on saved data size, not guaranteed.
release: Preparation only; no new FDTD or optimizer released
